q1_issues.issue: The trade is reified and asserted at top level as an occurring event, though the sentence names it only as what the coin is used for, and the oblique-object rule keeps a bare noun as a constant, i.e. (For sk_use_1 trade).
(Agent sk_trade_1 sk_villagers_1) gives the villagers a role in a trading event the sentence never predicates of them.

(Inheritance outside_merchant outside) exposes an attributive-only modifier that fails the predication test ('the merchant is outside' does not mean 'from outside'), so the genus merchant should stand alone.

q2_gaps: purpose/ground 'for'-PP whose object is an eventuality noun carrying its own comitative argument ('for trade with outside merchants') - the preposition-named oblique takes a bare constant object and offers no slot for the 'with' phrase
notes: The definite-plural group event plus the per-member distribution rule for 'the villagers use coin' follows the grouped-plural doctrine correctly, at the right strength and confidence.
